I will keep my land in the usual wheat-maize rotation. In Quzhou County, this is the cropping pattern I trust most because it matches the local climate, the soil, the water conditions, and the way I already know how to farm. I want steady yield and steady cash flow, not extra risk. So I will keep winter wheat on the land through harvest, then I will follow it with summer maize. I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed because I care more about stable production and disease resistance than saving on seed. I will not spread my land across too many crops, because that makes field work, fertilizer timing, irrigation, and pest control harder to manage.

For management, I will fertilize wheat a bit heavier because it needs strong tillering and grain filling, and I will split nitrogen so I do not waste it all at once. I will irrigate wheat at the key stages because spring moisture is not something I want to gamble on. After wheat harvest, I will get maize in quickly so I do not lose heat and moisture. For maize, I will keep fertilizer moderate and focus on seedling establishment, jointing, and grain filling. I will use ploughing before wheat because I want a clean, solid seedbed, and for maize I will use rotary tillage after wheat harvest because it is faster and fits the short turnaround. I will spray only as much as I think is needed to keep weeds, aphids, rust, armyworm, and other common problems under control while protecting yield.
